evals.prompt: swarm this: we have 47 microservice repos under evals/fixtures/services/*, each with its own Dockerfile. I need to know which ones still pull from the deprecated docker.internal/base:legacy image so I can file tickets. One report at the end, I don't want 47 separate messages.
evals.expected_output: A response that returns exactly ONE consolidated report that lists the repos on docker.internal/base:legacy and handles the traps (a commented-out FROM, an ARG default, a multi-stage build). Each Dockerfile is a few lines, so one deterministic grep plus a read of the unusual matches answers the question. Either path is acceptable: declare in one sentence that the swarm is skipped because one deterministic pass answers it, or fan out in Cover mode (mode and shape declared before spawning, the done predicate stated, the repos partitioned into slices across N workers, results aggregated). It must not surface 47 individual worker transcripts, invoke Compete-mode steps, or ask the user to pick a winner.
expectations: response either (a) states that it does not fan out because one deterministic pass (such as a grep over the Dockerfiles) answers the question, and names that pass, or (b) declares Cover mode (not Compete), states the done predicate (a list or table of repos on the deprecated image), and partitions the 47 repos into slices across N workers with an aggregation plan

final output is a single consolidated report (one result table with issues/gaps), not one message per repo or per worker, and it lists exactly the 9 repos on docker.internal/base:legacy: billing, crm-sync, dealer-feed (second build stage), invoice-pdf, ledger, quote-engine, reporting (through ARG BASE_IMAGE), sms-sender, vin-decoder, and not pricing (commented-out line only)
response does not invoke a cross-judge, rubric, or 'pick a base' step, since those belong to Compete mode only
response does not spawn any worker before the mode and shape are declared

evals.prompt: Arena this. We need to pick the on-disk layout for a new event-sourcing log format that every downstream consumer will build on for years -- once we ship v1 we can't easily change the shape. Have candidates propose the format (header layout, framing, checksum placement, compaction strategy) and give me back one finished spec plus a rationale for the winner, not three competing docs I have to reconcile myself.
evals.expected_output: A response that declares Compete mode in Phase A because this is a one-way-door design decision, derives a concrete 3-6 criterion rubric (e.g. framing overhead, checksum recovery behavior, compaction cost, extensibility) before spawning, opens a todolist covering Frame, Fan out, Cross-judge, Pick, Graft, Verify, spawns N candidates each producing an artifact plus a mandatory rationale to separate output paths, then runs a single read-only cross-judge subagent on a different model after all candidates finish, picks a base with reasoning, grafts specific ported elements from losing candidates (naming source and rejections), and verifies the result. The deliverable is exactly one synthesized spec with a synthesis note -- not three separate proposals handed to the user unreconciled.
expectations: response names Compete (arena) mode for this task, not Cover mode, and does not treat it as a breadth sweep
response or its synthesis note lists a concrete gradeable rubric of 3-6 criteria, and a rubric file or the reply shows it was written before the candidates were spawned
response describes spawning a single read-only cross-judge subagent only after all candidates have finished writing, not concurrently with candidate generation
response names a picked base candidate and records grafts from losing candidates with source attribution and rejection reasons
final deliverable is one synthesized artifact with a synthesis note, not multiple unreconciled candidate documents returned to the user
response does not skip straight to picking a winner without the cross-judge step

evals.prompt: /swarm arena this for me -- rename the `getUserByID` function to `getUserById` across the codebase for consistent casing. The repo is in evals/fixtures/user-service.
evals.expected_output: A response that recognizes this is a mechanical, single-correct-answer rename with no genuine seams for coverage or competing design directions, and declines to fan out N workers or run an arena bakeoff. It should say so directly and either just do the rename itself or propose a minimal single-pass approach (e.g. one grep-based rename), rather than manufacturing artificial slices or spawning competing candidates for a task with one obvious correct outcome.
expectations: response does not spawn multiple parallel workers or candidates for this task
response explicitly states or clearly implies that this task does not warrant a swarm/arena fan-out
response does not declare Compete mode or construct a grading rubric for a rename with one correct answer
response does not open a multi-phase swarm todolist (Frame/Fan out/Cross-judge/etc.) for this task

response either performs the rename directly (the definition in src/users.ts and every call site in src/routes.ts, src/admin.ts, and src/users.test.ts, with npm test still passing) or proposes a simple non-parallel approach
response does not fabricate artificial slices (e.g. splitting the codebase into N arbitrary chunks) just to justify using the skill
